items.feedback: Not quite. You picked 'Flat on the food, with the fingers stretched out', which leaves your fingertips in the blade's path; the right answer is b, a claw with the fingertips curled back. Say you slice a carrot into 5 mm rounds: with flat fingers, a slip puts the edge on a fingertip, but with a claw the first thing it meets is a knuckle.
Right. The knuckles guide the side of the blade, so the fingertips never meet it. Keep your knuckles forward and the blade rides along them as you slice.

Not quite. 'So the knife does not slip' is about the knife, but the curl is about your fingers: it tucks the fingertips back so the knuckles take the side of the blade. Say the blade skids while you cut a carrot into 5 mm rounds: the knife can still slip, but it hits a knuckle and not a fingertip.

summary: You know the knuckles guide the side of the blade. The thing to fix is why the claw grip works: it keeps your fingertips out of the blade's path, and it isn't there to stop the knife slipping. Next time you cut a carrot, curl your fingertips back and say out loud which part of your hand the blade is touching.
